answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote on a task or claim rewards. The protocol caps each stake’s influence, then slashes it when independently audited work is fraudulent or duplicated. Creating a thousand names no longer creates a thousand cheap votes: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it. A small ember of fraud can trigger a ripple of audits, while the stake and audit trail provide a signal that makes repeated Sybil attempts increasingly costly.
